note: Built cross-index: 1757 IRQ registrations, 1333 unique handlers, 1112 resolved defs, 211 handler-def sites with plain spin_lock, 83 handler-plain-lock x same-file-other-site pairs (cross.tsv.json). Korina confirmed.

candidates.reason: korina_tx() called from hardirq korina_tx_dma_interrupt (request_irq:1004) takes lp->lock with plain spin_lock at 526 with IRQs enabled; sibling hardirqs korina_und_interrupt:935 and korina_ovr_interrupt:962 also take it plainly; nested same-CPU IRQ preempts holder and spins forever. Underflow/overflow interrupts are attacker-triggerable via TX activity (underflow: ETH_TX_UND stat at 566).
candidates.conclusion: korina lp->lock plain in three hardirq handlers -> nested-IRQ same-CPU spin deadlock, unbounded interrupt-context lockup.

candidates.reason: hardirq m32r_sio_interrupt (request_irq:541) takes up->port.lock plainly at 477 while holding i->lock plainly (466); its helper receive_chars drops/re-takes port.lock plainly (381/384-386). The same port lock is taken plainly by timer-softirq callback m32r_sio_timeout at 577, which runs with hard IRQs enabled (timer softirq) when port has no hw IRQ (startup:634 mod_timer). A UART RX hardirq on a sibling port (shared irq_info chain) preempting the timeout's critical section spins forever on up->port.lock held by softirq that cannot resume. Non-hw-IRQ port requires CONFIG_SERIAL_M32R_PLDSIO/M32R platform; do_timer path uses m32r_sio_handle_port, same helper.
candidates.conclusion: m32r_sio port->lock taken plainly by both hardirq handler (477) and timer-softirq timeout (577); hardirq preempting softirq holder self-deadlocks.

candidates.reason: tx/rx/top FEC IRQs are three separate hardirq handlers, all plain; xmit path uses irqsave; no non-irq-context plain holder of priv->lock (timeout hw_reset uses irqsave). Nested-hardirq pair only.
candidates.conclusion: nested-hardirq-only plain lock; no process/softirq holder; not this branch.

candidates.reason: netdev_error and netdev_tx_done plain acquisitions at 1127-1163 are all inside hardirq intr_handler; no other same-file plain site of np->lock.
candidates.conclusion: plain lock sites are all inside the single hardirq handler; no non-irq holder.

candidates.reason: atp_timed_checker (722) and atp_interrupt (605) are the only plain users; TIMED_CHECKER block is #if 0-disabled at re-arm (693) and the checker never re-arms itself on s04; timer only runs if #if 1 block taken; also parallel-port NIC.
candidates.conclusion: timer callback is effectively disabled (#if 0 re-arm); no live non-irq plain holder.

candidates.reason: llc_restart_tx unlocks DriverLock before send_queued_packets and relocks after; netif_start_queue runs unlocked; no plain DriverLock acquisition outside skfp_interrupt (489); other sites are irqsave.
candidates.conclusion: no non-irq-context plain acquisition of DriverLock; unlock-during-work pattern avoids the hazard.

candidates.reason: ql_disable_completion_interrupt takes qdev->hw_lock plainly (672). Need caller-context audit: if any process-context caller (open/close/ethtool) runs with IRQs enabled while qlge_isr hardirq (2502, plain) can preempt, it is reportable; if only called from hardirq/napi contexts it is nested-irq-only like korina.
candidates.conclusion: trace all callers of ql_disable_completion_interrupt in qlge_main.c and classify context; process-context caller would confirm defect.

candidates.reason: msm_irq (306) plain, helper handle_rx (166/217/224) plain, console __msm_console_write (867) plain. msm console write occurs during earlycon/oops/panic where IRQs off or system halted; earlycon port is not the IRQ-driven runtime port (separate earlycon device); set_termios uses irqsave (525). Known-lockdown console semantics; not attacker-influenced.
candidates.conclusion: console/earlycon-only plain acquisitions outside hardirq; no attacker-triggerable process-context holder.
